findings.diagnosis: The prompt underweights high-contradiction signals: scorers rank positions with strong contradiction probabilities too highly when cohesion looks acceptable, letting single high-contra cuts zero the set.
findings.evidence: ['ja_jp_1211','ja_jp_918','ja_jp_773','ja_jp_1159','ja_jp_1325','ja_jp_740','ja_jp_1562','ja_jp_1257'] — in each case the policy kept a cut with very high contra (≈0.92–0.999) that destroyed the H_set.

edit.text: If a cut's contra ≥ 0.90, treat it as effectively catastrophic: rank it at the bottom regardless of cohesion and avoid keeping such cuts.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt applies a categorical prohibition on 'internal splits' (particles/bound morphemes) that is too strict for very short‑latency settings, causing scorers to thin needed dense boundaries and lose short‑bin performance.
findings.evidence: ['ja_jp_1211','ja_jp_773','ja_jp_740','ja_jp_918','ja_jp_1159','ja_jp_1325'] — these short/≤5‑latency cases show targets placing denser early cuts (including adjacent to particles/morpheme boundaries) that the policy avoided, improving H_set.

edit.text: In very short‑latency (dense) settings, allow cuts adjacent to particles or bound‑morpheme boundaries when the left fragment alone is coherent and non‑contradictory; do not forbid them categorically.
